title: Canonical normal Stein model over a Noetherian base
statement: Let $f:T\to B$ be a proper dominant morphism of integral Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Here Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover whose section rings are Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and dominant means that the image is dense. Assume that every local ring of $T$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. There exist an integral scheme $S$ and dominant morphisms $g:T\to S$, $q:S\to B$ with $f=q\circ g$, such that every local ring of $S$ is an integrally closed domain, $q$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and $g$ is proper with geometrically connected fibres [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. This is the canonical relative spectrum $S=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_B(f_*\mathcal O_T)$, specified by the following charts and maps: for every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], put $U=f^{-1}V$ and $R_V=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_T)$. Then $q^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}R_V$, the ring $R_V$ is a finite $A$-module, $q$ is induced by $f^\sharp:A\to R_V$, and $g|_U:U\to\operatorname{Spec}R_V$ is the evaluation morphism (its pullback on global sections is the identity of $R_V$ under the affine spectrum identification).

proof.text: By [pqf-lem-proper-basic], $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization] to obtain $T\xrightarrow{g}S\xrightarrow{q}B$, with $f=q\circ g$, $q$ integral, $g$ dominant and $S$ integral. On $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq B$ its affine chart is the spectrum of the integral closure $A'_V$ of $A$ in $R_V=\Gamma(f^{-1}V,\mathcal O_T)$, and the map on sections induced by $g$ is the inclusion $A'_V\hookrightarrow R_V$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-normal-stalks]: its hypotheses are exactly quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of $f$, integrality of $T$, and the assumed integrally closed domain stalks of $T$. Thus all stalks of $S$ are integrally closed domains.

source.place: Tag 03H0, proof using the relative normalization; morphisms.tex Tags 035H, 035I and 035L (lemma-normal-normalization).

proof.text: The given finite Noetherian affine covers make $T$ and $B$ locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. On an affine chart $\mathcal O_T$ is $\widetilde A$ and is generated by $1$, hence is quasi-coherent of finite type [pqf-def-coherent]. Therefore [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] makes $\mathcal O_T$ coherent. Apply [lem-pc-coherent-hi] to the proper $f$, the locally Noetherian base $B$ and this coherent module, in degree zero: $f_*\mathcal O_T$ is coherent. For every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $B$, [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-affine-sections-finite] gives that $\Gamma(V,f_*\mathcal O_T)=R_V$ is a finite $A$-module. This proves the required finiteness on every affine chart, not merely on the selected Noetherian cover.

source.place: Tag 01XZ (lemma-coherent-Noetherian), Tag 02O5 (proposition-proper-pushforward-coherent), and Tag 01PB, used in Tag 03H0 proof.

proof.text: Fix an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq B$ and put $U=f^{-1}V$. The restriction $f_V:U\to V$ is proper by the base-change clause of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-stein-factorization-affine] to $f_V$: the induced $A\to R_V$ is integral, and the evaluation morphism $U\to\operatorname{Spec}R_V$ is proper with geometrically connected fibres. Every element of $R_V$ is therefore integral over $A$, so the subring $A'_V$ in step 1 is all of $R_V$. The chart and map clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization] now identify $q^{-1}V$ with $\operatorname{Spec}R_V$, $q$ with the spectrum of $f^\sharp$, and the pullback of $g|_U:U\to q^{-1}V\cong\operatorname{Spec}R_V$ on global sections with the identity of $R_V$ (the inclusion $A'_V\hookrightarrow R_V$ has become the identity). By [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction] a morphism $U\to\operatorname{Spec}R_V$ is determined by its pullback on global sections, so $g|_U$ is exactly the canonical evaluation morphism $U\to\operatorname{Spec}H^0(U,\mathcal O_U)$ of the Stein factorization of $f_V$, and the properness and geometric connectedness just quoted hold for $g|_U$.

source.place: Tag 03H0, proof and properties (1)--(5); Tag 03H2 over an affine base; morphisms.tex Tag 01W4 (lemma-base-change-proper) and Tags 035F, 035H, 035I.

proof.text: The relative normalization of step 1 is $\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_B(\mathcal O\prime)$, where $\mathcal O\prime\subseteq f_*\mathcal O_T$ is the integral-closure algebra [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization]. Step 3 proves equality of these algebra sheaves on every affine open; the sheaf gluing axiom then gives $\mathcal O\prime=f_*\mathcal O_T$. Consequently this very $S$ is the asserted canonical relative spectrum, with the global maps already constructed in step 1. Since $q$ is integral, it is affine, and step 2 makes every chart ring $R_V$ finite over $A$; hence $q$ is finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Finally $f(T)\subseteq q(S)$ and $f(T)$ is dense in $B$, so $q$ is dominant. The dominance of $g$ was obtained in step 1.

The opens $W_V=q^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}R_V$ cover $S$, and step 3 identifies $g^{-1}W_V\to W_V$ with a proper map. Properness assembles from its definition [def-weil-proper-morphism]: $g$ is universally closed by [lem-weil-pbc-universally-closed-zariski-local] applied to the open cover $W_V$ of $S$. The diagonal is a closed immersion because its restrictions over the open cover $W_V$ are the proper local diagonals (the defining closed-subscheme ideals glue). Local finite type is checked on the same affine charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Quasi-compactness follows by covering any affine open $W\subseteq S$ by finitely many affine principal subopens lying in members of this cover; the inverse image of each is quasi-compact by local properness. Thus $g$ is separated, of finite type and universally closed, hence proper.

source.place: Tag 01W2 (lemma-proper-local-on-the-base), elementary open-cover verification of the definition.

proof.text: For a point $s\in S$, choose an affine $V\subseteq B$ containing $q(s)$. The fibre of $g$ over $s$, and its base changes to extension fields of $\kappa(s)$, are exactly those of $g|_{f^{-1}V}:f^{-1}V\to q^{-1}V$. The identification follows by the fibre-product defining equations: the map from any scheme over $s$ already factors through the open $q^{-1}V$. This restricted morphism is the evaluation map of step 3, so [lem-weil-pbc-stein-factorization-affine] gives geometrically connected fibres. This holds for every $s$, completing all clauses.
